palette: Lapis night-blue and slate-blue shadows, warm cream paper highlights, oxblood-red cloth accents, pale olive-green hillsides; molten gold is the ONLY saturated warm colour in any frame, so the metal always pops; electrum drawn pale butter-yellow, silver cool grey.
light: Low raking late-afternoon sun (and furnace fire for the refinery) as a single warm key from one side, cool blue ambient fill, crisp warm rim light on silhouettes and metal; deep blue cast shadows, no teal.
style_string: Flat 2D storybook illustration with bold simplified shapes and clean confident edges, soft two-tone cel shading, subtle visible paper grain, painted in a restrained palette of lapis night-blue and slate-blue shadows, warm cream highlights, oxblood-red accents and pale olive-green hills, with molten gold as the only saturated warm colour; low raking warm key light from one side, cool blue ambient fill, crisp warm rim light; strong readable silhouettes, one clear focal subject filling the upper two thirds of a vertical 9:16 frame, distinct foreground, midground and background layers for parallax, Iron Age western Anatolia around 550 BCE. No text, no letters, no watermark, no border.

cast.look: a lean Lydian trader about 40 years old, sharp hooked nose, short curly black beard, black hair tied back with a thin oxblood-red headband, knee-length undyed cream wool tunic with an oxblood-red hem border, bare forearms, plain brown leather sandals

a broad heavy-set refiner about 55 years old, shaved head, thick short grey beard, soot-smudged cheeks, sleeveless slate-blue knee-length work tunic belted with rope, brown leather apron, bare feet, thick forearms

King Croesus, about 35 years old, tall and upright, long dark ringlet hair and long curled black beard, plain smooth gold band diadem, ankle-length deep purple robe with a narrow gold border, heavy plain gold bracelets

notes: 18 shots is the cap. Lines 3 and 6 (7 words, about 2.3-2.6 s at Shorts pace) get one shot each with strong motion; every other line over 2.5 s gets two. Captions sit at 66% height: keep key subjects in the upper two thirds. Proof beats: s03 (line 2, ~2.1 s), s16 (line 12, ~1.5 s), s18 (line 14, ~1.9 s, last image = real coin, loops into s01 coin-into-palm). All coins drawn as small irregular oval lumps, never rimmed discs.

shots.see: Trader's face, three-quarter view, frozen mid-step: he pinches the pale lump between thumb and forefinger right in front of one narrowed eye, other brow lifted in doubt; blurred market awning and steep acropolis hill behind in cool blue (trader).

Frame 0, action already happening: a small irregular pale butter-yellow electrum lump caught mid-fall a finger-width above the trader's open calloused palm, a short warm motion streak above it, fingers already starting to curl; oxblood tunic hem edge and dark lapis background, hard warm rim light on the lump. Only the trader's hand and wrist (trader).
The Met 26.59.2 gold stater photo, whole coin, on its plain dark background; slams in at 110% scale and settles, gentle warm glint sweep.

Low angle from below: the trader, waist up, holds a small bright pure-gold oval lump high against the low sun between thumb and forefinger, gold blazing with rays, his face lit warm in awe; deep blue sky and the acropolis hill silhouette behind (trader).

Top-down extreme close-up of one irregular oval lump made of swirled bands of gold and cool grey silver, like marbled stone, split by a clean crack down the middle: left half glowing gold, right half dull silver-grey, resting on dark blue wool cloth. No people.
the grey silver half of the same lump

Wide from a low angle in the Sardis market: the trader large in the foreground at his stall, one fist raised on each side holding a lump, one deep gold and one pale washed-out yellow, shrugging; behind him mudbrick-and-stone houses with tiled roofs, the steep acropolis and the river Pactolus, two or three distant figures only (trader).

Eye-level close shot of a bronze hand balance held up by the trader's fist on the beam: a pale lump in one pan and a small stone weight in the other, beam tilted; the trader's doubtful eye blurred at frame edge (trader).

Ground-level angle across a flat black touchstone: a fresh pale-yellow streak in sharp focus in the foreground, the trader's fingertips still dragging the lump across it; behind, out of focus, his squinting face leaning over the stone (trader).

High angle looking down: the refiner kneels by a coarse brown clay pot filled with white salt and red brick dust, pressing thin pale electrum sheets into it with both partly closed hands; beside him a reed basket of salt; beyond, the river Pactolus and the acropolis of Sardis in cool evening blue (refiner).

Low wide angle at dusk: a row of three small dome-shaped mudbrick ovens glowing orange from their mouths, the refiner a strong dark silhouette sliding one lidded clay pot into the nearest with a long wooden paddle, sparks drifting into a deep blue sky (refiner).
Top-down extreme close-up of a cracked-open clay pot: a flaky grey-white crust peeling back like bark and pale wisps of vapour lifting off, revealing bright gold sheets shining underneath. No people.

Low angle close: the refiner's cupped, partly closed palm in the foreground holding a small heap of bright gold grains glinting, his soot-smudged bearded face above lit warm gold from below, a slow proud smile; dark blue workshop behind (refiner).
Eye-level medium, square to camera: the trader, waist up, arms folded, one eyebrow raised high, staring straight into the lens; plain cool blue wall behind for a clean silhouette (trader).

Side angle at anvil height, the instant of impact: the refiner's thick soot-smudged forearm and fist on a short iron hammer slamming down on a square bronze punch sitting on a small gold oval blank on a stone anvil; a burst of warm sparks; only forearm and hand visible (refiner).

Top-down close on the stone anvil: two small freshly struck irregular oval lumps side by side, left one bright gold, right one cool silver, both with the same simple lion-face-and-bull-face relief, the punch just lifting out of frame; no labels or marks of writing. No people.
The Met 26.59.2 photo cropped tight on the relief: starts on the lion forepart and pans across to the bull forepart, showing the real stamp.

Low wide angle in a columned stone hall with deep blue shadows: Croesus rising slightly from a carved wooden throne, one hand on his chest, inclining his head in a modest bow toward camera, a single warm shaft of light on him and his gold bracelets (croesus).

The Met 26.59.2 gold stater photo, whole coin on its dark background, starting tight and slowly pulling back to show the whole small lump; final image of the video, loops into s01's coin landing in the palm.
